overview: The City Council and Community Development Board held a joint meeting to review revised zoning amendments for Medford Square, focusing on district boundaries, height limits, and historic preservation incentives. Both bodies voted to continue the public hearing to April 21, 2026, while coordinating final technical adjustments to parking and daylighting standards.

items.title: Approval of Records
items.summary: Approved the records of the special joint meeting held on March 3, 2026.

items.title: Hearing 26023: Medford Square Zoning Amendments
items.summary: Reviewed proposed amendments to Chapter 94 regarding Medford Square zoning, featuring a presentation on revised sub-district maps and dimensional standards.

items.title: Zoning Map and Height Standards Discussion
items.summary: Discussed boundary changes including the removal of certain residential parcels and height reductions in sub-districts MS1 and MS2 to protect historic and residential contexts.

items.title: Parking, Incentives, and Historic Preservation
items.summary: Evaluated new incentive structures for community solar, public parking, and the adaptive reuse of historic buildings, including a proposed 'daylight minimum' to protect sun access for neighbors.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Heard testimony regarding the need for more commercial focus over residential density, the saturation of banks in the Square, and the impact of government-mandated parking minimums on housing affordability.

items.title: Hearing Continuation and Procedural Timeline
items.summary: Voted to continue the public hearing to April 21, 2026, to allow consultants to incorporate specific technical tweaks into a final draft before a final Council vote scheduled for late April.

items.title: Item 26058: Medford Square City Hall Overlay District
items.summary: Briefly introduced the 'Transom' project overlay district for discussion, noting that detailed zoning waivers and design introductions will be presented at the next joint meeting.

subject: Medford Square Zoning Amendments Review
